subject: skill name
rationale: user chose to avoid rename churn; content reframing carries the new meaning

subject: artifact storage location
rationale: ships in the same tree gh-pages mirrors; uncluttered repo root; signals 'project-state alongside project-docs'

subject: severity tier model
chosen: 4-tier (FYI / Fix / Block / Override) with label-encoded distinction
rationale: captures the real oversight verbs: notes, corrections, stop-signals, risk-acceptance; mandatory Override logging provides durable human-decision capture

subject: schema field name for agent identity
rationale: Codex flagged inconsistency in pass 2; agent_id matches the path convention docs/agent-state/<agent_id>/

subject: build-time freshness persistence
chosen: CI commits claims.json back to main with bot author + [bot] prefix
rationale: reproducibility from main's history outweighs commit-noise; modes are mutually exclusive with agent-write-time to prevent write conflicts

subject: dogfood auth mode
chosen: public-passthrough (no client auth; overlay opens prefilled github.com/issues/new in new tab; reads via unauthenticated GitHub API)
rationale: public repo + solo collaborator; pass-through is zero-infra and avoids token UX entirely; documents a missing third mode in the methodology
evidence: user message: This is a public repo so no need to login

subject: promote public-passthrough to a documented third auth mode in build-html-dashboard
chosen: add as Phase 1a option + full row in Auth modes table + pattern-2/7 caveats in Phase 5 + simpler /docs-on-main deploy in Phase 6
alternatives: rewrite Phase 5 to abstract over auth modes
rationale: dogfood validated the approach works end-to-end; without documenting it, other public-repo projects will reinvent it or fall back to PAT/OAuth unnecessarily

subject: multi-agent overhead handling in methodology
chosen: Phase 1b adds 'when to split vs collapse' + 'cross-agent rendering' guidance; default per-agent for ≤3, unified above. Trust Calibration always per-agent.
rationale: Codex flagged 'no guidance on when to collapse roles or aggregate pages' as a new problem; collapsing by default keeps schema cost down for small projects

subject: comment-overlay load-bearing patterns count
chosen: expand from 10 to 15 patterns: add 11 (decouple overlay walk from page render lifecycle via dashboard:rendered event + unwrap-before-rewrap), 12 (position-preserving whitespace-flexible regex fallback), 13 (saturated 4-tier highlight palette including indigo FYI), 14 (#N marker pills next to each anchor), 15 (capture-phase click handler with preventDefault + unanchored-comments banner)
alternatives: leave as 10 patterns and put the new 5 in a 'pitfalls' section
treat patterns 11-15 as v2-specific and version-tag them
rationale: These cure specific failure modes discovered the hard way in the v2 dogfood (same provenance as the original 10 from imagehide). Putting them in a 'pitfalls' section would understate their load-bearingness and make them easier to skip during implementation.

subject: dogfood-before-publish requirement in methodology
chosen: Add 'Dogfood before publishing' section to build-html-dashboard with a 5-step verification checklist (build → file each tier → verify highlights + markers + clicks → file cross-section → refresh + re-walk). The original 10 came from imagehide's real use; 11–15 came from this dogfood's. Future patterns will only come from real use.
alternatives: require Codex spec-review as the verification step (insufficient — Codex passed the spec twice and didn't catch 11-15)
rationale: Two-round Codex spec review did NOT catch the implementation race conditions, coordinate-space bugs, or visibility-against-real-backgrounds issues. Spec review and dogfood are complementary, not substitutable. Future projects following the methodology should dogfood before declaring it 'done'.
evidence: codex pass 2 (5 blockers, none mentioned timing/visibility)
dogfood surfaced 5 new patterns within minutes of real use

subject: comment display UX — saturated highlights + #N markers vs subtle highlights + click-popover
chosen: Subtle severity-tinted highlight (alpha 0.10 + dashed 1px border-bottom) + click-to-reveal popover with note text. No marker pills. Unanchored becomes a small collapsed pill bottom-right, expands to a list on click.
alternatives: hybrid: subtle highlight + tiny dot marker
rationale: User feedback: 'The comment display mode is wrong, it should hide at first, only highlight the words with comment, and click to pop the comment.' Real-use insight beats my initial guess that markers are needed for discoverability. The dashboard surface is the product; comments are metadata about it. Saturated highlights would turn a busy oversight surface into a heat map. Subtle highlight signals 'comment here' without dominating; the popover gives full context on demand.
